insight.title: How the Invisible Becomes Our New Horizon
insight.subtitle: Moving from cold glass screens to a world that breathes with us.

sections.text: For a long time, we looked at the future through glass. We held cold rectangles and tapped at pixels. But the walls between our dreams and our living rooms are beginning to fade. Tomorrow does not look like a machine. It looks like a room that understands your quietest needs.

Soon, intelligence will be like the morning light. It will be woven into the wood of your table and the threads of your coat. Sensors will feel like a soft pulse, not a circuit. Technology is finally learning to speak the language of touch, texture, and the human spirit.

This shift returns our eyes to the horizon. We will stop looking down at our palms and start looking at each other again. Life becomes seamless once more. When the digital world finally behaves like nature, we will realize that the greatest innovation was always our very own human presence.

news.title: Improving cartilage repair through cell therapy
news.description: A new method can monitor iron in cells known as mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), which can help determine their ability to grow tissue for cartilage repair. The breakthrough could lead to regenerative therapies for joint diseases.
